findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_sessions.py, hook_command(): f"{sys.executable} {script} hook --provider {provider} --state-dir {state_dir}". Use shlex.quote on each part. _is_ours() matches on the HOOK_MARKER substring, so quoting is compatible with detection as long as the marker text stays contiguous.
findings.summary: The rendered hook command interpolates the interpreter, script and state-dir paths without shell quoting. A path containing a space, for example a macOS home directory, produces a command that fails on every event. Each failure exits 1 and the registry silently goes stale.

findings.evidence: agent_sessions.py ingest(): `started(pid)` is called once for a new record, then twice more in the `previous.get("pid_started") != started(pid)` check and the following `record.update(pid=pid, pid_started=started(pid))`. Compute it once per event and reuse it. Better, only re-probe when `previous.get("pid") != pid`.
findings.summary: The design says tool-event hooks stay cheap, but ingest() runs `ps` up to three times per event. Every PreToolUse and PostToolUse also pays a Python start-up plus an fsync'd write.

findings.evidence: agent_sessions.py list_sessions(): `record = read_record(path)` and `view(...)` are not guarded per file. read_record raises on JSON errors or a version mismatch, and _parse raises on a bad timestamp. lifecycle_overview.read_sessions then returns {"error":...,"sessions":[]}. Consider skipping and reporting the bad file while still listing the rest.
findings.summary: A single corrupt or invalid session file makes list_sessions raise. The overview then reports the whole registry as unreadable and hides all healthy sessions. A bad `updated_at` has the same effect, because view() calls _parse and that raises SessionError.

findings.evidence: lifecycle_overview.py read_sessions(): `raise OverviewError(f"[agent_sessions] {key} must be set ...")`. overview(), show_pr() and show_requirement() call it unguarded.
findings.summary: An incomplete `[agent_sessions]` section raises OverviewError from read_sessions. That aborts the entire lifecycle overview, including the PR and Requirement views, instead of degrading to the explicit session-status line the registry-unreadable case uses.

findings.evidence: agent_sessions.py main(): `ingest(..., pid=os.getppid())`. liveness() returns `gone` when the pid is missing or its start time differs, and view() then forces state="ended". design.md Risks covers only the 'never a false working' direction.
findings.summary: The session root pid is taken as os.getppid() of the hook, and it is re-recorded on every event when it differs. If the hook runs under a short-lived shell, or a Codex notify wrapper, the recorded process dies quickly. A live, working session is then shown `ended (process-gone)`, which is a false negative. The design only argues that a false `working` is impossible.

findings.evidence: docs/engineering/agent-sessions.md, 'Codex' section, plus the argparse definition `hook.add_argument("--payload-json", ...)` in agent_sessions.py. The `hooks` subcommand renders only CLAUDE_EVENTS.
findings.summary: Codex ingestion has no render or install path, and the docs do not show the `notify` configuration. The CLI needs an explicit `--payload-json` flag as the final argument, whereas the docs say Codex passes the payload as the last argument. Operators cannot wire Codex from the docs alone.
